sources.title: When will Modern Warfare 4 be on Game Pass?
sources.text: COD: MW4 will be on Game Pass, but not at launch Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 (2026) will not be on Xbox Game Pass at launch, which may came as a point of frustration to those COD fans who were hoping that the company's involvement with Microsoft would mean a day-one Game Pass availability. However, that doesn't mean that it's not coming at some point in the future, as I'll lay out the details below. According to an official press release from the development team, Modern Warfare 4 is not going to be available on Xbox Game Pass until "Holiday 2027," roughly one year after its initial launch and release. Further details about exactly when in the year that will be are currently not available, but either way players can expect a long wait if they're dependant on Game Pass and don't want to purchase a copy for themselves. MW4 will still be available to buy on Xbox from its initial launch date of October 23, 2026, but not on the Game Pass subscription service. If you want an alternative until then, there are still a multitude of Call of Duty games currently available on Xbox Game Pass to download as part of the service, going all the way back to Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War from 2020. Alternatively, if you're less brand-loyal and just want to find an online military shooter to experience with friends, Battlefield 6 is also available for free on Game Pass. © GamesRadar+. sources.title: Dragon Quest Monsters: The Withered World details online content, offline Battle Arena, and Wrangler’s Gauntlet
sources.text: Publisher and developer Square Enix , and developer TOSE have released new information and screenshots for Dragon Quest Monsters: The Withered World introducing online content, the offline Battle Arena, and the new roguelike mode Wrangler’s Gauntlet. ■ Team Up With Wranglers the World Over and Take on Joint Battles Together! After you progress some way through the story of Dragon Quest Monsters: The Withered World , you’ll unlock a host of online content. These modes are enabled for cross-platform play, meaning you can enjoy them with anyone, regardless of their chosen gaming system. One of those modes is Online Joint Battles, where you can team up with other wranglers to test your skills against massive monsters together. There are daily quests to try your hand at, as well as special events featuring infamous monsters from across the Dragon Quest series, with fantastic rewards for those able to overcome the challenge! —With three difficulties of regular quests to choose from, you can select the level of challenge that best matches your current party’s strength. —Once you’ve chosen the quest you want to take on, you can start the matching process to find other players. You can also choose to play alone if you wish. —During battle, you can talk with your teammates using a selection of simple preset messages—and you’ll need to communicate if you want to emerge victorious! —When you use healing and support skills on allied parties in battle, you’ll boost your collective Team Bonus. This multiplier increases the damage that everyone can inflict on the enemy and boosts the effectiveness of healing abilities. —Keep an eye out for super-tough Special Quests that feature special monsters. These events regularly come and go, so be sure to give them a try if you’re feeling strong enough. You can earn monster eggs as rewards for completing Online Joint Battles and other challenges. The monsters that hatch forth can then be added to your party! —Eggs come in four colors, and all sorts of monsters can be inside. ■ Connect Online to Access a Wealth of Extra Content! In addition to Online Joint Battles, connecting online allows you to battle against other players in Ranked Matches to improve your global ranking, fight parties that players have uploaded via the Wranglers Society and much more. However, because the online content, such as Online Joint Battles and Ranked Matches, is intended to be a fair test of your monster wrangling skills, the Wrangler’s Spirit ability won’t activate in these game modes. —In Ranked Matches, you compete against other players of a similar ability to yours. There are seven main ranks, from Beginner to Legendary, and the goal is to rise as far you can in the standings. —Every victory rewards you with Ranking Points. Your total at the end of a season determines your rank. Perform well and you might earn promotion to a higher rank, with rewards for doing so! —In Private Matches, you can customize the rules of battle, such as setting the number of rounds or the times you can swap in your reserves. —Head over to the Online Hub, where other players are represented, to participate in the Wranglers Society. By speaking to the wranglers there, you can battle against their parties, so be sure to take your strongest monsters along with you. —Win a battle in the Wranglers Society and you’ll get to spin the roulette wheel to determine your reward, with items, mini medals and other great prizes up for grabs. —The Online Shop has some valuable items for sale. The lineup changes depending on the day of the week and your progress through the story, so check back regularly to see what new stock has come in. ■ The Battle Arena, Where Monster Wranglers Go to Test Their Mettle! In addition to the online content, there’s also a fully offline Battle Arena to enjoy, which Bianca and Nera will discover upon visiting Witherwood Castle. In these contests, you’ll send the monsters you’ve raised into battles that will determine the strongest wrangler in the kingdom. This Battle Arena features both regular battles and joint battles, each with seven difficulty categories from G up to A. With rewards on offer for completing a category, the Battle Arena is the perfect place to test your skills or take a break from adventuring. —In the regular Arena Battles, you have to win all three matches in a category to complete it. Your monsters’ HP and MP will be fully restored between matches, so you can always fight to the max. Once you pay the entry fee, it’s time to start battling! —During battle, you can choose the general tactics you want your monsters to follow. Keep close tabs on how each battle plays out and adjust your tactics accordingly. —In Joint Battles at the arena, you can set the tactics for your main party and your reserves, as well as for the other monster wranglers who fight alongside you. ■ An All-New Roguelike Mode for Extended Replayability! Progress even further through the story and a new challenge will unlock in the Battle Arena called the “Wrangler’s Gauntlet” that will truly test your ability as a monster wrangler! Devised by Scruffy, the Wrangler’s Gauntlet provides you with a selection of monsters that changes each time you attempt the challenge. You must use what you’re given to build a party capable of winning 50 consecutive battles. The monsters you befriend here, and the items you obtain, can’t be taken out on your adventures, but with different starting monsters each time and opponents that change with every new attempt, no two runs are ever the same. The roguelike elements offer a fresh perspective on monster wrangling! —The challenge begins once you receive your monsters from Scruffy. He’ll even tell you which monsters you’ll face off against in the next battle, meaning you can tailor your party to best deal with each different opponent. —After winning a battle, you’ll have the opportunity to strengthen your party. sources.name: Polygon
sources.title: Star Wars Zero Company Finally Makes Starting A New Campaign Worth It
sources.text: There has never been a better time to play Star Wars Zero Company I've been waiting for a reason to start a new playthrough of Star Wars Zero Company ever since I beat the game in early September. EA and Bit Reactor have finally given me a reason to come back to the game, as Patch 1.2 added a lot of new gameplay settings that will allow me to tweak my next playthrough's difficulty to my liking. Star Wars Zero Company was an excellent XCOM-like tactics game, but there wasn't much else to mess around with after beating the game once. Players had to turn to mods for more detailed campaign settings, as post-launch updates were nearly nonexistent after Bit Reactor furloughed many developers before release. Bit Reactor brought back some furloughed workers earlier this month and subsequently released Patch 1.2, which goes beyond simple bug fixes. The update includes gameplay tweaks to encourage Upgrade Facility use and make Cly's Combat Jump movement ability less overpowered. The most exciting additions are a plethora of campaign modifiers that let players tweak a campaign's difficulty. Keep in mind that you do have to turn these settings on before you start a new playthrough; they currently can't be changed mid-campaign. It's typically pretty hard for units to die in Zero Company , as they had to be injured three times in one mission. It's now officially possible to turn on "Instant Death" so units die after one injury, or "Two Strikes" so they die after two injuries. Alternatively, players sticking with the three-injury setup can enable a static or escalating "risk of death," which adds a chance that units die when injured. You can also remove or disable health increases from earning Focus Points, disable cross-training for disliked pairs, or reduce the advantage gained from different attack types. Perhaps my favorite new setting is "No Perfect Shots," which adds to the chaos by making it so the maximum chance to hit for any attack is 99%. All these new settings can make Star Wars Zero Company much harder, even on its standard difficulty, and are exactly the kind of modifiers that can draw me back to replay a tactics game. I'm definitely looking forward to a playthrough with the Instant Death and No Perfect Shots settings turned on in the near future. Star Wars Zero Company Update 1.2 is live now across PlayStation 5, Windows PC, and Xbox Series X. Bit Reactor also teased that it plans to "explore additional configurations in future updates" for campaign modifiers. If you want to read through the whole list of patch notes in more detail to learn more about every single campaign setting you can now tweak, character nerfs and buffs, and bug fixes, this is what EA and Bit Reactor shared, sans developer notes: The Call For Backup ability can now be bound to a hotkey of your choice.

sources.name: Gematsu
sources.title: Dementium II coming to Steam on October 20
sources.text: Atooi will release horror first-person shooter sequel Dementium II for PC via Steam on October 20, the developer announced. Dementium II first launched for DS on May 4, 2010, followed by PC on December 17, 2013. The Steam release is a new, “remastered” version. Here is an overview of the game, via its Steam page : The DS horror sequel, reborn. William Redmoor wakes with fresh staples in his skull, inside an institution for the criminally insane, where the walls keep peeling back to expose something worse. Fight, solve, and survive your way out. The cult classic, remastered. The last thing William Redmoor remembers is the Doctor’s scalpel. Now he wakes at the Bright Dawn Treatment Center with a new wound and an old accusation: the records say he murdered his wife. In his cell, a postcard is waiting. The handwriting is his own. It tells him to run. The staff insist he’s recovering. But since the surgery, reality has started to split, and the “hospital” keeps tearing open into a demented version of itself. The Doctor has a theory about why: whatever was wrong inside your head, we let it out! Escaping Bright Dawn is only the beginning. Outside lies an empty village and a countryside crawling with things that shouldn’t exist. Letters signed by his wife lead him deeper. She says she’s waiting for him. Faithful to the Original. Rebuilt for Today You don’t need to have played the first game to survive this one. Here’s what you need to know. In Dementium: The Ward , William Redmoor woke up in a hospital with no memory, surrounded by creatures that had no business being alive. Newspaper clippings claimed he had murdered his wife. Visions of his daughter led him deeper into the dark, while a man in black who called himself the Doctor watched every step. William fought his way down to the basement to face him. It didn’t end the way he hoped. Dementium II begins where that ending left him: under the Doctor’s knife.

sources.title: Fortnite is coming to Linux so we may soon be able to play it and other games like Apex Legends on Steam Deck and Steam Machine
sources.text: Epic Games is officially working on bringing its battle royale shooter Fortnite to Linux. The announcement was tucked away at the bottom of Epic's widely mocked blog post revealing the new, "vibe-coded" Epic Games Store, which is also coming to Linux. At the time, Epic explained it's going to be working with Linux distro maintainers on a set of security requirements needed to run Fortnite. Distros - short for distributions - are operating system variants of Linux, each with its own goals and prioritised system operations. Valve's SteamOS, for instance, is based on Arch Linux. Because of the many discrepancies between Linux distros, each would need to implement Epic's security requirements individually if they want Fortnite to run on their operating system. Fortnite will arrive on Linux via the EGS launcher, but only if a "critical mass of distro maintainers" is reached. Epic didn't specify numbers. This is big news for several reasons. For one, the move would likely make Fortnite playable on SteamOS PCs and handhelds, including Steam Machine and Steam Deck. Furthermore, even if that "critical mass" is never reached, Epic says its work will be available to other developers interested in bringing their games to Linux. Perhaps the biggest reason this is a big deal, however, has to do with Easy Anti-Cheat, the Epic-owned anti-cheat service used in Fortnite and dozens of other games - including Dead by Daylight , Rocket League , Apex Legends , and even Elden Ring . While Easy Anti-Cheat does support Linux, including for some of the games just mentioned, many developers choose not to enable it , simply because its "Linux implementation couldn't offer the same level of protection as our Windows implementation," as Epic explained in a separate blog post . This is why many games that use Easy Anti-Cheat aren't playable on Steam Machine or Steam Deck . The post even names Valve specifically, saying the team will "continue its open line of communication" to support Steam hardware devices "to the maximum extent technically possible". Part of the reason Linux has been a difficult problem for anti-cheat makers to solve is the platform's open nature, meaning certain - required - system-level protections are not guaranteed. On Windows, you can ask users to enable features like TPM 2.0 and Secure Boot , which create that secure environment once hardware requirements are met. While some of that work can be done on Linux, it requires the interest and participation of distro maintainers. Easy Anti-Cheat plans to use Linux features such as signed kernel, signed kernel modules, and secure boot with attestation to achieve that goal. "These requirements build on work that distribution maintainers already do," explains Epic, "and the more distributions that meet these requirements by default, the fewer players will need to change their setup to play." The goal is to "bring the level of protection much closer to par with Windows". There is no timeline for any of this at present, but Easy Anti-Cheat will test the announced plans in Fortnite first before making them available to other developers. In other words, if Fortnite gets a release date on Linux, you'll know the work has paid off and we're closer than ever to achieving anti-cheat parity between Windows and Linux.

sources.text: Retroware has released a new gameplay trailer for side-scrolling beat ’em up game Toxic Crusaders . Here is an overview of the game, via its Steam page : When the evil Dr. Killemoff attacks, only one team of hideously deformed creatures of superhuman size and strength stands between him and his plans for global pollution: the Toxic Crusaders, earth’s last, greatest and ugliest hope for survival! The hottest heroes of 1991 return for a radical, radioactive beat ’em up for a new era, featuring awesome action, crushing combos and more toxic waste than you’ll know what to do with! Choose from seven playable characters, including Toxie, No-Zone, Junkyard, Major Disaster and Headbanger (who would technically count as two characters if they could only agree on something)—plus, for the first time, play as Toxie’s musically “gifted” girlfriend Yvonne, and the mother of all mothers, Mrs. Junko, Toxie’s mom! Battle across seven disgusting levels rendered in beautiful full-color pixel art as you defend Tromaville from hordes of Radiation Rangers, mutated thugs and zombie chickens. The odds might be stacked against you but with awesome powers, a winning personality and up to four-player local co-up on your side, the Smogulan Empire’s days are numbered! Take a deep breath and dive deep into an action-packed, pun-filled adventure that drags you kicking and screaming through the wonderful world of Troma. Enjoy cameos from gore-filled classics such as Class of Nuke ‘Em High, Poultrygeist: Night of the Chicken Dead, and Sgt. Kabukiman N.Y.P.D.—reimagined in the Saturday morning cartoon style that made this franchise so unforgettable! Toxic Crusaders is due out for PlayStation 5 , Xbox Series , PlayStation 4 , Xbox One , Switch , and PC via Steam in 2026.

sources.name: GamesIndustry.biz
sources.title: Sega and Creative Assembly remove Total War: Shogun 2 remaster from sale as it "falls short of both your expectations and our own standards"
sources.text: Recently launched title has received overwhelmingly negative reviews on Steam, with players citing AI upscaling and performance issues Sega and Creative Assembly have temporarily withdrawn Total War: Shogun 2 – Complete Edition from sale in response to concerns about AI upscaling and other performance issues. Since its October 13 launch, the remaster has received overwhelmingly negative reviews on Steam. Players have reported that assets such as unit cards and new cutscenes display AI-generated features , including extra fingers and armor merging into characters' bodies. As described on Steam , the "underlying graphics technology has been brought to modern standards to take advantage of new methods in rendering," resulting in improved graphics and textures. In response, both companies issued a joint statement acknowledging that the game "has fallen short of both your expectations and our own standards." "We've seen your feedback, comments, and reviews. We agree that the current experience is not where it needs to be." "As a result we are working with platform holders to temporarily remove the game from sale and to reinstate the original game while we investigate the issues. Existing owners will still be able to access and play the game." "We are working closely with our development partner to identify the causes of these problems, deliver improvements, and ensure Shogun 2 – Complete Edition meets the quality standards players expect from Total War." Earlier this year, Sega faced criticism for its use of generative AI in Crazy Taxi: World Tour. The game's Steam page included a generative AI disclaimer, which clarified that Sega uses the technology "as a support tool for developers, aiming to provide better content to our users and enable developers to focus more on creative tasks." "We have used such generative AI support tools during development of Crazy Taxi: World Tour. No AI was used in reference to the performers in game." In a statement to Game Informer , Sega clarified that generative AI was "used to support our teams during the development of background assets" and that "assets generated were still subject to review by the development team."

sources.name: The Verge Games
sources.title: Sega pulls Total War: Shogun 2 remaster from sale following disastrous launch
sources.text: Total War: Shogun 2 — Complete Edition is being removed after users discovered bugs and upscaling that appears to have been done by AI. Total War: Shogun 2 — Complete Edition is being removed after users discovered bugs and upscaling that appears to have been done by AI. If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement. Sega is removing Total War: Shogun 2 — Complete Edition from storefronts following a disastrous launch where users complained about issues like bugs and upscaling that appears to have been done by AI. Complete Edition , a remaster of the 2011 strategy game, launched on Tuesday, and it bundled the main game and all of its DLC with promised upgrades including “improved visuals,” “1440p and 4K UI scaling,” and modernized controls. It has an “Overwhelmingly Negative” rating on Steam , where it has already been pulled, and posts on Reddit showcase artwork that users believe AI messed up. “We’re aware that Total War: Shogun 2 – Complete Edition has fallen short of both your expectations and our own standards,” Sega and developer Creative Assembly wrote in a post . “We’ve seen your feedback, comments, and reviews. We agree that the current experience is not where it needs to be.” The two companies say they will “reinstate the original game,” and existing owners will “still be able to access ” Complete Edition . Sega and Creative Assembly say that they are “working closely with our development partner to identify the causes of these problems, deliver improvements, and ensure Shogun 2 - Complete Edition meets the quality standards players expect from Total War.” A studio called Mataboo is also listed as a developer for the game on Steam, and Mataboo highlights its work on the game on its website .

sources.title: Gamescom Asia x Thailand Game Show 2026 announces four additional pavilions from Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, and the US
sources.text: This year's event will host 29 countries and regions, described as "most international line-up in show's history" Gamescom Asia x Thailand Game Show 2026 has announced four additional pavilions, bringing its total to 20 from 12 markets across Asia, Europe, and North America. Newly announced pavilions include Indonesia (Ministry of Creative Economy), Japan (JETRO), Malaysia (Malaysia Digital Economy Corporation), and the US (US Embassy Bangkok). These join the already established pavilions from Austria, Germany, the Philippines, South Korea, Spain, and host nation Thailand. South Korea will bring six delegations led by KOCCA and regional agencies from Busan, Daejeon, and Jeonnam. Additional delegations will come from Japan (CANTEEN and MIXI Global Investments), China (Gamirror Games), and Taiwan (Taipei Computer Association). Overall, this year's Gamescom Asia x Thailand Game Show will host exhibitors from 29 countries and regions, described as "the most international line-up in the show's history." "National pavilions only get backing when there is a clear business case. For the German games industry, Gamescom Asia x Thailand Game Show is exactly that," said Game managing director Felix Falk. "This is where East meets West in games. For Asian developers, it is the most direct route to international partners. For Western studios, it is the front door to some of the world's fastest-growing games markets." Thai Games Association president Kittipong Prucksa-aroon added: "As representatives of the host nation's association, we look forward to bringing the region together at Gamescom Asia x Thailand Game Show, together with other major ASEAN country pavilions from Indonesia, Malaysia and the Philippines. "With that, Gamescom Asia x Thailand Game Show has truly become the regional meeting point for Southeast Asia's games industry. There is no other place where Southeast Asia's leading games markets come together at this scale, under one roof, alongside the world's major gaming nations. Prucksa-aroon concluded: "For developers, publishers, investors and players, that makes Bangkok the place to be and see where Southeast Asian gaming is heading next." This year's event takes place from October 29 to November 1 at the Queen Sirikit National Convention Centre (QSNCC). As previously announced, Gamescom Asia x Thailand Game Show's exhibitor lineup includes Capcom, Bandai Namco, and The Pokémon Company, as well as Nintendo and PlayStation represented by partners. Additional exhibitors include 4Divinity, Elementa, Gryphline, Kuro Games, Razer, AMD, Lenovo, and others. The business area will be open from October 29 to October 30, exclusively to games industry professionals and media. It will feature a conference with more than 80 speakers from 27 countries, headlined by John Romero with a keynote entitled "Why We Still Make Games".
